title: Open-model compatibility gaps and integration effort estimates
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Objective: Produce a prioritized catalog of open-model providers (weights: enterprise readiness, latency/cost profile, licensing, regional availability) with a slot-based estimate of engineering integration effort for Redwood deployments (Hosted API, Dedicated, Private).

Scope:
- Evaluate 12 candidate open models and 6 provider distributions (cloud-hosted variants, third-party optimizers, quantized builds).
- For each provider-model pair, assess compatibility across four axes: API/format compatibility, quantization/tooling support, runtime kernel and operator coverage, and legal/licensing constraints.
- Produce an effort estimate (S/M/L/XL mapped to 1/3/8/20 engineering days) for integrating each provider into Redwood's serving/runtime and Console (model catalog + rollout controls).

Deliverables:
1) Integration matrix CSV with columns: provider, model, api_surface_gaps, kernel_coverage_pct, quantization_supported, estimated_days, blockers, recommended_work_archetype.
2) A short memo (Confluence) with top 5 strategic recommendations and trade-offs (e.g., prioritize providers that reduce latency in EU region vs. providers that require heavy kernel backfill).
3) Engineering RFC seeds for 3 prioritized integrations (one Hosted-focused, one Dedicated throughput-focused, one Private/VPC enterprise-focused).

Methodology:
- Static analysis of provider artifacts (API contracts, model weights, quantization docs).
- Quick local smoke runs (where license allows) to validate KV cache behavior and streaming semantics.
- Interviews with 3 existing vendor partners to validate hidden operational costs (e.g., model refresh cadence, hotfix cadence).
- Cross-check with Runtime and Infra leads to estimate kernel gaps (ENG-3421) and packaging/upgrade implications (ENG-3570).

Success criteria:
- Integration matrix completed for >=90% of targeted pairs.
- Top 3 integrations have clear, scoped RFCs and committed ENG owners.
- Executive memo with recommended prioritization and estimated incremental cost/year for each high-priority integration.
acceptance_criteria: Matrix CSV uploaded to Drive and linked in Confluence memo
At least one RFC draft created per prioritized integration
Work estimates reviewed and endorsed by Runtime and Infra leads
Risks and licensing flags enumerated with mitigation suggestions
